note: research/reporting-inventory-main.md at 93334b8 (inside the D-93 public stamp), section C; Edith's ruling on the kept group-C items: ops/reviews/2026-10-13-study1b-plan-and-groupC.md (958894b), Part 2. Conventions from research/reporting-definitions-main.md (93334b8), items 1-24 and Addenda A-C4. C1, C4, C6, C8 and C12 are dropped, C11 is a sentence only and C13 is a later run: none is computed here.

C10-1.choice: <pair> is spelt "opus-low-vs-opus-med" and "haiku-low-vs-haiku-med", <shape> "6x1" / "1x6": seeds derive_seed(20261011, "effort:opus-low-vs-opus-med:6x1") and so on. The call is report_arms._paired (bootstrap.paired_bca, margin -10, B 10,000, seed derive_seed(20261011, name)), as item 10 uses it.
C10-1.why: X1: main_rows arm names; C1 9h: the "<a>-vs-<b>" form of a pair.

C10-2.choice: as_deployed only. Per-base scores are scoring.arm_scores (official): "each over its tries" is the share right over the arm's tries (one try for Opus); the differences are scoring.paired_differences over the bases both arms have. Only d and the 95% interval are reported (no p, no reading).
C10-2.why: C1 item 10 pins as_deployed for exploratory differences against a comparator; the definition says "Report d and the 95% interval" and "No Holm, no verdict".

C10-3.choice: The cost difference is the difference of the two item 9b headline means (report_costs.cost_block: mean list cost per puzzle; a Haiku arm at one sample, i.e. its single try), arm minus comparator, in USD, a point value; each arm's 9b block (mean, median and their bands) is shown beside it.
C10-3.why: The definition says "cost difference from item 9b"; 9b's headline is the list-price mean; it gives no interval for the difference.

C2-1.choice: "Per arm" is every arm of the 80-base design (X5) that ran at both shapes: haiku-med, opus-med, opus-low, sonnet-med, haiku-low, haiku-thinking-off, haiku-max, sonnet-low. E3 is out (it ran at 1x6 only); the D-42 and real-time arms are out (X5).
C2-1.why: X5 defines "every arm" for items 7 and 24; a correlation across shapes needs both shapes.

C2-2.choice: Per-puzzle accuracy is scoring.arm_scores (official, as_deployed): a Haiku arm's share right over its tries (the designed tries, a missing try wrong), a one-try arm's 0 or 100. In points; r is unchanged by the scale.
C2-2.why: The same per-puzzle single-try accuracy items 12 and 24 report (I6).

C2-3.choice: r is the sample Pearson correlation, sum((x - mean x)(y - mean y)) / sqrt(sum((x - mean x)^2) sum((y - mean y)^2)), sums by math.fsum; in a bootstrap draw a base drawn twice enters twice. If either shape's values are all equal (for example Opus-medium right on every puzzle at one shape), r is "undefined (no variation)": the point estimate says so, and a draw where it happens is dropped and counted; the interval is over the kept draws, with the share dropped reported.
C2-3.why: The definition gives no rule for a constant variable. Addendum C4 item 3 is the reporting definitions' rule for a statistic with no value in a draw (0/0): dropped and counted, the interval over the kept draws, never withheld.

C3-1.choice: The arms of C2-1. A Haiku arm's "whole-answer accuracy" is its single-try accuracy (scoring.arm_scores), not a vote; d = the mean over bases of (6x1 score - 1x6 score), in points, and the interval is the shared cluster bootstrap's percentile interval of that mean (not BCa).
C3-1.why: The definition names no k, and "whole-answer accuracy" of an arm is the single-try value in items 12 and 24; it names the shared cluster bootstrap and "descriptive", so not the confirmatory BCa machinery.

C5-1.choice: k_O is each shape's own confirmatory k from k.json (test 1's k_O(6x1), test 2's k_O(1x6)); the per-base scores are exactly tests 1 and 2's (main_analysis._test_scores: five_tests.vote_scores at that k against five_tests.single_scores of Opus-medium); the value per base is (t1's difference) - (t2's difference), over the bases both tests have. If either k_O is 0, C5 is not computed.
C5-1.why: "For tests 1/2 only": the tests' own k and scores; k_O differs by shape (D-33, one k per shape).

C7-1.choice: Bins as item 20 step 1 (each puzzle's Haiku-medium single-try share over its 40 designed samples, a missing sample wrong; 10-point bins, the last including 100). "Per-bin" is the whole bin: all its puzzles together (item 20's thirds and its "too few wrong tries" group pooled). Item 20 step 3 is applied to the bin: the smallest k in 1..40 at which the bin's mean vote@k (item 8 curve, report_votes.arm_curve) reaches Opus-medium's mean accuracy on the same puzzles, "reaches" being >= after rounding both to 1e-9 (C1 item 20); else "none up to 40".
C7-1.why: The definition says "per-bin" (item 20 computes step 3 per cell); every other rule is item 20's and C1's.

C7-2.choice: "Within k_O" is k <= that shape's confirmatory k_O (k.json). The crossover, per shape, is the lowest bin (by its lower edge) whose smallest reaching k is within k_O; if no bin qualifies, "no bin reaches Opus within k_O". Every bin's values are listed beside it, so a non-monotone pattern is visible.
C7-2.why: k_O is per shape (D-33); the text sentence is per shape because the bins are.

C7-3.choice: No interval: the smallest k and the crossover are point values.
C7-3.why: X6: item 20's "smallest k reaching Opus" is a point value with no band; the C7 definition names no interval.

C9-1.choice: The arm is Haiku-medium. A puzzle's wrong-try agreement is item 20 step 2's per-puzzle share (item 4's pairing): unordered pairs of its WRONG real tries (kind "missing" left out) with an identical official vote key, a None key never agreeing (D-72.1), by scoring.pairwise_agreement.
C9-1.why: Item 4's share is Haiku-medium's; item 20 is the reporting definitions' per-puzzle use of it.

C9-2.choice: Vote gain = vote@k_O - single-try accuracy, in points: vote@k_O by five_tests.vote_scores at that shape's confirmatory k_O (k.json; official, as_deployed, tie "random"), single-try accuracy the share right over the 40 designed samples (main_analysis._per_puzzle_share, as item 20 step 1). If k_O is 0 at a shape, C9 is not computed there.
C9-2.why: k_O is per shape (D-33); the single-try share is item 20's.

C9-3.choice: Spearman's rho is the Pearson correlation (C2-3's formula) of the ranks, ties given their average (mid) rank; the values are rounded to 1e-9 before ranking so equal rationals tie. Ranks are recomputed within each bootstrap draw, a base drawn twice entering twice. If either variable is constant, rho is "undefined (no variation)", and such a draw is dropped and counted (C2-3).
C9-3.why: The definition names Spearman but no tie rule; mid-ranks are the standard form; the 1e-9 rounding is C1 item 20's rule for comparing such values; the undefined rule is C4 item 3's.

C9-4.choice: The bootstrap draws from the KEPT puzzles only (those with at least 2 wrong tries); the left-out puzzles are counted and listed.
C9-4.why: The left-out puzzles do not enter the statistic; X6 draws item 20's bands from the cell's own base puzzles in the same way.

G1.choice: The official score (D-76 with D-90's repeat rule) in the as_deployed view: a missing, refused, truncated or unparseable try is wrong and stays in its denominator.
G1.why: No definition names a score or a view. Addendum A: every statistic uses the official score unless the item says otherwise; as_deployed is the headline view, and the one items 1, 2, 9c and 20 and C1 item 10 (exploratory differences) use.

G2.choice: "Shared cluster bootstrap 95%" is Addendum A's shared convention: curve.cluster_bootstrap, 2,000 draws, base seed 20261012, percentile 95% (order statistics), base puzzles drawn with replacement, a drawn base bringing both its shapes, all its tries and all arms. Names (one per statistic, X1 style with main_rows arm names): "rho:<arm>" (C2), "shape_diff:<arm>" (C3), "shape_x_setup:haiku-med-vs-opus-med" (C5), "repeat_vs_gain:haiku-med:<shape>" (C9).
G2.why: The definitions name the shared bootstrap but no statistic names; X1 fixes the style (arm names, shapes 6x1 / 1x6).

G3.choice: "The 80 base puzzles" are the base puzzles the arm (or the paired arms) has rows for at the shapes used; with the driver's rows (planned tries with no record are rows of kind "missing") that is every base of the set.
G3.why: The driver's rows include every planned try, so this is the whole set; stated so the count is checked, not assumed.
